title: Check the game's data without launching it
text: A check that needs the game's data but not its picture runs the game's own code with no window and no world: data-check reads what the mod registered, each item as a real stack, and every error the game logs while it loads the data packs. It costs about 5 CPU-s per check once one loaded JVM answers many checks, instead of 49 for a hidden client.
result: mmt data-check works on Fabric 26.3: on the Prism Lab demo mod it lists the mod's items, blocks, loot table and recipe with no game launched, and a broken recipe fails it with the game's own error. The game stays loaded: a changed data file costs about 2 CPU-s in 2 s, copied from src without Gradle when Gradle would copy it as it is. A spare game waits behind it, started up to just before the mods' own code, and takes changed code for about 5 CPU-s in 4 s; a changed mixin or loader file loads a fresh game, 12 s. The build is read once and kept until a build file changes. A loaded game holds about 0.38 GB.
